title: The limits of Excel and when to move to a database or BI platform

videos.script: Everything in this course has happened inside one workbook, on one computer, for one person. That is where Excel is at its best. {{one}} This lesson is about the edges. A sheet has a last row. Past it, data does not arrive, and the warning appears once. {{edge}} A file has one owner at a time. Send it round by e-mail, and by Friday there are two versions. Neither of them is the truth. {{copies}} And when a spreadsheet is the only check, its mistakes become public. A health agency left thousands of positive tests out of its figures. An economics paper averaged the wrong rows. A bank's risk model was fed by copying and pasting. {{cases}} None of that makes Excel the wrong tool. Most questions are still best answered in it. What you need are the signals that a job has outgrown the file. {{signals}} And then, where to take it. A database, for data that many people write. A BI platform, for reports that many people read. This track teaches both, in the courses that come after this one. {{next}}
